title: Factors for Long-Term Ritodrine Monotherapy in the Treatment of Preterm Labor: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: Ritodrine is used to manage threatened preterm labor (TPL) in Japan. While short-term administration is recommended internationally, long-term administration remains the customary practice in Japan, creating a gap in clinical practice between Japan and other regions. This retrospective study aimed to identify the maternal factors associated with long-term administration of ritodrine monotherapy. We reviewed the records of patients who received ritodrine infusion for TPL at the Yamaguchi University Hospital between April 2017 and March 2023. Patients were classified into the long-term monotherapy group (n = 37) if they received ritodrine monotherapy for more than 2 weeks. The non-long-term monotherapy group (n = 102) included patients who received ritodrine monotherapy for less than 2 weeks, required additional tocolytic agents, or discontinued ritodrine due to adverse events. The analysis showed that the white blood cell (WBC) count at treatment initiation was significantly lower in the long-term monotherapy group (p < 0.05). A receiver operating characteristic curve analysis identified a WBC count of 8710 as the cut-off value for predicting long-term administration. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified a WBC count below 8710 at treatment initiation as an independent factor for the long-term administration of ritodrine infusion (odds ratio: 2.57; 95% confidence interval: 1.12-5.90). Although further validation is required, these findings suggest that the WBC count at the initiation of ritodrine infusion may serve as a potential indicator of long-term ritodrine monotherapy administration in pregnant women with TPL.

title: Inhibitory Effects of Gamma-Linolenic Acid on the Contractile Responses of Guinea Pig Ileal Longitudinal Smooth Muscle.
abstract: Gamma-linolenic acid (GLA), an n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid, has been reported to influence gastrointestinal function after prolonged exposure. However, its direct effects on gastrointestinal smooth muscle contractility remain unclear. We examined the effects of GLA on receptor-mediated and depolarization-induced contractions in the guinea pig ileal longitudinal smooth muscle (ILSM) and explored the underlying intracellular signaling mechanisms. GLA (10-60 μM) concentration-dependently inhibited acetylcholine (ACh)- and histamine-induced contractions, causing rightward shifts of the concentration-response curves and reductions in the maximal responses, with a greater rightward shift observed for ACh. Inhibition by 10-30 μM GLA was largely reversible, whereas that by 60 μM GLA was only partially reversible. GLA (30-60 μM) also suppressed 80 mM potassium chloride (KCl)-induced contractions. ACh- and histamine-induced contractions were sensitive to the L-type Ca2+ channel (LCC) inhibitor verapamil. However, in A7r5 cells, GLA (60 μM) did not attenuate the high-KCl-evoked Ca2+ elevation, which was sensitive to verapamil. In A7r5 cells, GLA reduced the phosphorylation of both myosin light chain (MLC) and myosin phosphatase target subunit 1 (MYPT1) under basal and depolarizing conditions. GLA also inhibited [3H]N-methylscopolamine binding to muscarinic receptors in the mouse cerebral cortex. Collectively, these findings suggest that GLA suppresses ILSM contraction through intracellular mechanisms downstream of Ca2+ entry, which are associated with reduced phosphorylation of MLC and MYPT1, while additional muscarinic receptor inhibition may contribute to the greater suppression of ACh-induced contraction.

title: [Reference guide for the clinical management of adult Langerhans cell histiocytosis (key points from the first edition, 2025)].
journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology
abstract: According to the registry of the Japanese Society of Hematology, adult histiocytic neoplasms are extremely rare, with approximately 40 cases reported annually, and the most common among them is Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH). Lesions may involve multiple organs, including bone, skin, lung, the central nervous system, and the endocrine system. Without a hematology perspective, the neoplastic nature of LCH may not be apparent, resulting in missed diagnoses. Central diabetes insipidus, anterior pituitary dysfunction, and LCH-associated neurodegeneration, once developed, often result in irreversible impairment. Because delayed therapeutic intervention can result in permanent organ damage, it is essential for hematologists to understand the "minimum initial management" required to protect patient outcomes. This review summarizes the key points of diagnosis and initial management in adult LCH based on the first edition of the Adult LCH Clinical Reference Guide (2025).

title: Rebisufligene etisparvovec: The first AAV9-mediated SGSH gene therapy approved for the treatment of mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIA (MPS IIIA).
abstract: Mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIA (MPS IIIA; Sanfilippo syndrome type A) is a rare lysosomal storage disorder caused by biallelic SGSH pathogenic variants that results in heparan sulfate accumulation and progressive neurodegeneration. Previously, treatment was limited to supportive care. In September 2026, the US Food and Drug Administration approved rebisufligene etisparvovec-hopf (FAYUVI), an adeno-associated virus serotype 9-mediated SGSH gene-addition therapy, for neurological manifestations in pediatric patients with preserved neurodevelopmental function. Evidence was primarily derived from the open-label Transpher A study, which compared 17 early-treated patients with 27 external natural history controls. Between 24 and 60 months of age, the model-estimated difference in the change in Bayley-III cognitive raw score was 23.5 points (95% confidence interval, 17.2-29.9), favoring treatment. Heparan sulfate levels in cerebrospinal fluid decreased by a mean of 57.1% at 24 months. Among patients receiving the recommended dose, elevated liver enzymes (85%) and vomiting (67%) were common; serious adverse events occurred in 18 of 33 patients across all dose levels. The approval of rebisufligene etisparvovec represents a landmark advance in the treatment of MPS IIIA, establishing the first disease-modifying gene therapy for this disorder and demonstrating the therapeutic potential of early intervention. Ongoing follow-up and postmarketing surveillance need to be conducted to establish the therapy's long-term efficacy, durability, and safety.

title: Two-Stage Estimation for Causal Inference Involving Semi-Continuous Exposures.
abstract: Methods for causal inference are well developed for binary and continuous exposures, but in many settings, the exposure has a substantial mass at zero-such exposures are called semi-continuous. We propose a general causal framework for such semi-continuous exposures, together with a two-stage estimation strategy. A two-part propensity structure is introduced for the semi-continuous exposure, with one component for exposure status (exposed vs unexposed) and another for the exposure level among those exposed, and incorporates both into a marginal structural model that disentangles the effects of exposure status and dose. The two-stage procedure sequentially targets the causal dose-response among exposed individuals and the causal effect of exposure status at a reference dose, allowing flexibility in the choice of propensity score methods in the second stage. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality for the resulting estimators, and characterize their limiting values under misspecification of the propensity score models. Simulation studies evaluate finite sample performance and robustness, and an application to a study of prenatal alcohol exposure and child cognition demonstrates how the proposed methods can be used to address a range of scientific questions about both exposure status and exposure intensity.

title: MoS2/Ti3C2 composite interface as an electrochemical platform for dopamine and ascorbic acid sensing.
abstract: The electrochemical quantification of dopamine (DA) and ascorbic acid (AA) is of great physiological importance. However, it remains challenging due to the sluggish electrode kinetics of both molecules, motivating the design of electrode materials with tailored interfacial properties. Here, a porous layered MoS2/Ti3C2 nanocomposite with in-situ grown MoS2 on Ti3C2 MXene is prepared via a facile hydrothermal route and evaluated as a modified electrode material for DA and AA sensing. Electrochemical characterization reveals that the composite substantially enhances the oxidation peak current for both analytes relative to pristine MoS2, indicating improved electrocatalytic activity. For individual detection, the composite electrode exhibits linear response ranges of 0.8-1.6 mM for DA and 0.7-3.3 mM for AA, with detection limits (S/N = 3) of 4.5 μM and 9.2 μM, respectively. The observed electrochemical performance is attributed to a synergistic mechanism: the highly conductive Ti3C2 framework supports rapid charge transfer, while the in-situ grown MoS2 nanosheets form a three-dimensional porous architecture that mitigates Ti3C2 restacking, increases the density of accessible active sites, and promotes analyte diffusion. These findings establish the MoS2/Ti3C2 nanocomposite as a promising material platform for continuing development in electrochemical biosensing, including application in decentralized diagnostics for neurological disorders.

title: Magnetic solid-phase extraction coupled with fluorescent lateral flow immunoassay for simultaneous on-site detection of methamphetamine, morphine, and ketamine in wastewater.
abstract: Wastewater-based epidemiology provides objective, non-invasive data on community drug use, but conventional ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) analysis is laboratory-based and time-consuming. Although fluorescent lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) offers a simple, rapid, and low-cost alternative for on-site screening, its direct application to wastewater is limited by low analyte concentrations and complex sample matrices. We developed a magnetic solid-phase extraction (MSPE)-LFIA platform based on polydopamine-coated magnetic nanoparticle adsorbents for simultaneous detection of methamphetamine, morphine, and ketamine in wastewater. By investigating the organic solvent compatibility of commercial LFIA strips and using an acidic eluent with low methanol content, the nitrogen blowdown reconstitution step was avoided. Under optimized conditions, the proposed method achieved limits of detection of 13.6, 14.4, and 50.8 ng L-1, offering 66-, 61-, and 45-fold higher sensitivity than direct LFIA, with recoveries of 86.8-115.7% and RSDs below 12.3%. The entire procedure was completed within 15 min without bulky instrumentation. The method was applied to real wastewater samples, and the results exhibited good consistency with UPLC-MS/MS and a lower false-negative rate (16.7%) compared with direct LFIA (100%). This work provides the first MSPE-LFIA platform for simultaneous on-site screening of methamphetamine, morphine, and ketamine in wastewater. This platform enabled direct eluate loading and eliminated the nitrogen blowdown step, thereby simplifying the workflow. Given its simplicity and low cost, it is expected to be applicable to multiplex detection of common illicit drugs or other hazardous organic pollutants in wastewater.

title: "Apple tree"-like AuNPs@enzyme microreactor: A reusable microfluidic paper-based analytical device for improved acetylcholinesterase inhibitors screening.
abstract: Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors are key therapeutic agents for neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, yet conventional screening of natural product inhibitors are often time-consuming, instrument-dependent, and limited in reusability. To address this, we developed a simple, colorimetric platform based on a reusable microfluidic paper-based analytical device integrated with Au nanoparticle (AuNPs)-mediated enzyme microreactors, coupled with smartphone-based RGB values (blue (B), green (G), and red (R) channel) analysis for rapid and on-site screening of AChE inhibitors from natural products. The microreactors feature an "apple tree"-like architecture, in which AuNPs serve as the "fruits" enabling high-density oriented enzyme immobilization, enhanced substrate accessibility, and excellent reusability. AChE was oriented immobilized on concanavalin A-modified AuNPs surface via affinity self-assembly, achieving an 8.6-fold increase in enzyme loading compared to direct adsorption. The immobilized enzyme retained 87.0% of its initial activity after 80 consecutive assays, demonstrating excellent reusability and stability. The method showed superior repeatability with intraday, interday, and batch-to-batch relative standard deviations (RSD) of the colorimetric readouts all below 1.0%. The system enabled visual, quantitative evaluation during bioassay-guided fractionation, substantially reducing unnecessary separation steps. Moreover, half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC50) values of seven compounds from natural products were determined, correlating well with the reference UV method, confirming the reliability for practical inhibitor screening. This platform offers a cost-effective, reusable, and user-friendly tool for early-stage screening of AChE inhibitors in natural extracts, with potential to accelerate the discovery of lead compounds for neurodegenerative disease therapy while minimizing resource consumption and analytical workload.

title: CCA, a cassane diterpene from Caesalpinia bonduc ameliorates cognition impairment in Alzheimer's disease mice by regulating neuroinflammation and autophagy.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a severe neurodegenerative disorder, with persistent neuroinflammation and impaired autophagy recognized as key contributing factors. CCA is a naturally occurring cassane diterpene compound derived from the seed of Caesalpinia bonduc. Our research is the first to explore the role and mechanism of CCA in treating Alzheimer's disease. We assessed the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines and autophagy in BV2 cells following lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treatment and anti-neuroinflammatory effects of CCA were evaluated in LPS-induced mice, with the underlying mechanisms explored using transcriptomic. Additionally, we examined the cognitive-enhancing effects of CCA in APP/PS1 mice and investigated Caesalpinia bonduc associated molecular mechanisms through proteomic analysis, immunohistochemistry (IHC) and immunofluorescence (IF) assays. Finally, the molecular target of CCA was validated using molecular dynamics simulations and cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA). CCA can down-regulate the mRNA levels of inflammatory factors in BV2 cells stimulated by LPS, and has good permeability of blood-brain barrier. Furthermore, CCA ameliorated cognitive impairment and neuronal damage in both LPS-induced and APP/PS1 mice. And demonstrated that CCA mitigates neuroinflammation by driving microglial polarization from M1 to M2, a process potentially mediated by the AMPK/NF-κB pathway, thereby reducing tau pathology. Proteomic profiling and IHC revealed that CCA upregulates FOXG1 expression in APP/PS1 mice. Furthermore, the scTenifoldKnk confirmed that AMPK has a significant impact on the regulation of autophagy and inflammation response. Our findings verified that CCA exhibits anti-neuroinflammatory activity by AMPK/NF-κB pathway and activates autophagy via the AMPK-mTOR-FOXG1 signaling axis, which underscores its potential as a novel therapeutic option for the treatment of AD.

title: Quercetin activates lysosomal function to ameliorate neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits in chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
abstract: Chronic cerebral hypoperfusion (CCH) is a major contributor to vascular cognitive impairment (VCI), often resulting in progressive learning and memory deficits. Quercetin (Qu), a natural flavonoid with potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, demonstrates neuroprotective potential against ischemic injury, yet its mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. In this study, a rat model of CCH was established by bilateral common carotid artery occlusion, followed by Qu administration at doses of 20, 40, and 80 mg·kg-1. In parallel, HT22 cells subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD) were treated with Qu at 5, 10, or 20 μmol·L-1. Behavioral tests, histological staining, ELISA, and Western blot were used to assess cognitive performance, neuronal injury, lysosomal activity, NF-κB pathway activation, and inflammatory cytokine levels. Hippocampal RNA sequencing was also performed. Our results demonstrate that Qu greatly improved cognitive performance and attenuated neuronal damage in both the cerebral cortex and hippocampus. Mechanistically, Qu improved lysosomal function and suppressed NF-κB-mediated neuroinflammatory response, leading to less production of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Notably, co-administration of a lysosomal inhibitor attenuated the neuroprotective effects of Qu, underscoring the functional importance of lysosomal activation. In conclusion, Qu alleviates CCH-induced cognitive decline and neurodegeneration by restoring lysosomal function and inhibiting NF-κB-driven neuroinflammation. These findings support the therapeutic potential of Qu for VCI and provide a rationale for its further development as a neuroprotective agent.

title: Quercetin reverses the breast cancer-promoting effects of depression by targeting PPARγ.
abstract: Breast cancer (BC) has become the most prevalent cancer worldwide, and BC patients have the highest rate of depression of all cancer patients. However, previous studies, especially studies based on clinical sample data, have failed to reveal exactly how depression affects BC. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (TSMR) was used to determine the causal relationship between depression and BC. Transcriptomics and metabolomics were used to analyze BC samples from nondepressed and depressed patients and to validate differentially expressed genes and key metabolites in vitro. Molecular docking techniques were used to identify compounds that regulate key targets and validate the functions of the compounds in in vitro and in vivo animal models. Depression was identified as a risk factor for BC by the TSMR analysis. On the basis of clinical samples, for the first time, we identified PPARγ and norepinephrine (NE) as key genes and metabolites that mediate the pro-BC effects of depression. In addition, we demonstrated that quercetin can target PPARγ and reverse the procancer effects of PPARγ inhibition mediated by chronic stress in BC cells. Moreover, we found that PPARγ may be associated with the inhibition of CD8+ T cells in the tumor immune microenvironment. In conclusion, depression can increase the infiltration level of NE in tumors and inhibit the expression of PPARγ in tumor cells, thus promoting the proliferation of BC cells and inhibiting the infiltration of CD8+ T cells in the immune microenvironment, ultimately leading to accelerated tumor growth. Quercetin can target PPARγ and reverse this cancer-promoting process.

title: Integrated management of uterine prolapse during pregnancy: Case report and literature review of successful term delivery following cervical cerclage and pessary utilization.
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach for managing uterine prolapse during first-trimester pregnancy complicated by poor obstetric history. A prophylactic cervical cerclage and an adjunctive ring pessary were used to maintain cervical integrity and achieve successful term delivery. A 43-year-old woman, Gravida 12, Para 2, with a history of recurrent pregnancy losses, including a second-trimester loss attributable to cervical incompetence, presented with stage III uterine prolapse at 11 weeks of gestation. Prophylactic McDonald cerclage was performed at 12 weeks, after which a ring pessary and vaginal progesterone were utilized. The pregnancy was successfully managed to term, resulting in vaginal delivery at 38 + 5 weeks of a baby with birth weight of 2790 g and an Apgar score of 9/9. This case highlights the successful use of cervical cerclage and a pessary for managing uterine prolapse complicated by cervical incompetence during pregnancy, emphasizing the need for personalized management strategies.

title: Learning from Error Predictions Rather Than Prediction Errors: A Perspective on Self-Supervised Learning in the Brain.
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
abstract: Humans learn by doing and observing but also by imagining the result of simulated actions in their mind. When learning from executed or observed actions, traditional theories posit that behavior improves by minimizing the difference between (1) the perceived outcome derived from sensory feedback and (2) the desired outcome (performance error) or the outcome predicted by an internal model (prediction error, PE). Supporting these theories, decades of electrophysiological studies have documented the role of the dopaminergic system and cerebellum in generating activity patterns compatible with the hypothesized error signals. In comparison, our understanding of the neural basis underlying the ability to learn from simulated actions is far more limited. Here, I argue that this form of self-supervised learning is best described in terms of a quantity known as the predicted performance error (PPE), theorized more than 30 years ago and yet largely overlooked ever since. Complementary to PEs, PPEs reflect "error predictions" between predicted and desired outcomes. Unlike PEs, however, PPEs exist even in the absence of sensory feedback and can in principle serve to evaluate actions without executing them, based on an efference copy of the underlying motor plan. I review evidence supporting the computation of PPEs in the brain and propose a network implementation based on a cortico-basal ganglia loop interacting at multiple timescales with prefrontal, parietal, and hippocampal areas. I then connect PPEs to recent discoveries on motor planning and formulate novel predictions linking PPEs to various high-level brain functions such as metacognition, problem-solving, and deception.
